landmarks.name: Vilnius Old Town
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site known for its well-preserved medieval architecture and vibrant cultural scene.

landmarks.name: Trakai Island Castle
landmarks.writeup: A historic 14th-century castle located on an island in Lake Galvn, symbolizing Lithuania's medieval heritage.

landmarks.name: Hill of Crosses
landmarks.writeup: A pilgrimage site featuring thousands of crosses, representing Lithuanian faith and resistance.

cultural_events.name: Joninns (Midsummer Festival)
cultural_events.writeup: A traditional celebration marking the summer solstice with bonfires, singing, and dancing.

cultural_events.name: Kaziuko Mugn (St. Casimir's Fair)
cultural_events.writeup: An annual folk arts and crafts fair held in Vilnius, celebrating Lithuanian culture and heritage.

food_writeup: Lithuanian cuisine features hearty dishes such as cepelinai (potato dumplings), kugelis (potato pudding), and cold beet soup, reflecting the country's agricultural traditions and seasonal ingredients.
brief_history: Lithuania was a powerful medieval state, later forming a commonwealth with Poland. It was occupied by the Soviet Union in the 20th century and regained independence in 1990, becoming a member of the EU and NATO.

important_people.name: Vytautas the Great
important_people.description: Grand Duke who expanded the Grand Duchy of Lithuania.

important_people.name: Adamkus Valdas
important_people.description: Former President known for leading Lithuania through post-Soviet transition.

current_conflicts: Lithuania is not involved in any active military conflicts but maintains heightened security concerns due to regional tensions with Russia.
